newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes firmer as U.S. dollar softens.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes firmer as U.S. dollar softens.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed firmer on Monday mainly in response to a softer U.S. dollar.
Dealers expect settled trade until Tuesday morning around 8.30 a.m. (1930 GMT) when Treasurer Winston Peters is due to give a breakfast speech to Wellington businessmen.
The kiwi closed at 5.00 p.m. (0400 GMT) at US$0.6865/72 after opening at 0.6859/66.
Dealers said it was looking soft in the weekend at 0.6820 but the sharp fall of the U.S. dollar after the weekend G-7 meeting buoyed the kiwi.
"The dollar coming off gave a little bit of impetus," said a Wellington dealer.
He said there was selling of kiwi when the Trade-Weighted Index approached 68.10. the index ended at 68.05 from its 68.16 opening.
